Locally, docker-compose exposes Postgres itself on 5432 with no pooler, so the problems below only show up after deploy. The pool is sized at 20 server connections per service, and long transactions starve checkout, so keep transactions short and never hold one open across an HTTP call to the ledger. The pooler runs in transaction mode: session state does not survive between transactions (no SET session variables, no advisory locks across transactions, no LISTEN/NOTIFY), and server-side prepared statements fail with 'prepared statement does not exist'. With psycopg 3 you must connect with `prepare_threshold=None` to turn automatic prepared statements off.

./.engramdb/memories/database-connections-in-deployed-environments_01a106a2-baae-7832-8bf2-aff119eb37fd.md:15:In production and staging the app never connects to Postgres directly; every connection goes through a pooler on port 6432 that the platform team manages. Locally, docker-compose exposes Postgres itself on 5432 with no pooler, so the problems below only show up after deploy. The pool is sized at 20 server connections per service, and long transactions starve checkout, so keep transactions short and never hold one open across an HTTP call to the ledger. The pooler runs in transaction mode: session state does not survive between transactions (no SET session variables, no advisory locks across transactions, no LISTEN/NOTIFY), and server-side prepared statements fail with 'prepared statement does not exist'. With psycopg 3 you must connect with `prepare_threshold=None` to turn automatic prepared statements off.

I added `src/db.py`. It compiles, but I haven't run it against a real database.

```python
def get_conn():
    return psycopg.connect(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"], prepare_threshold=None)
```

- **`prepare_threshold=None`:** a project note says production and staging connect through a pooler on port 6432. That pooler breaks psycopg 3's automatic prepared statements with "prepared statement does not exist". Local docker-compose connects straight to Postgres, so you'd only see the error after deploying. Turning prepared statements off avoids it, and a comment in the code explains why.
- **Missing `DATABASE_URL`:** it raises a `KeyError` right away instead of quietly falling back to a default.
- **Dependency:** I added `psycopg>=3.1` to `pyproject.toml`. It wasn't listed before; only `tests/test_db.py` used it, and that test skips itself when psycopg isn't installed.

The same note also applies to code that uses these connections: the pooler doesn't keep session state between transactions. So no `SET` session variables, no advisory locks across transactions, and no LISTEN/NOTIFY. It also says to keep transactions short.

A memory hook flagged my `pyproject.toml` edit as possibly invalidating the "Route decorators in the API blueprints" memory. Adding a dependency doesn't touch route decorators, so I left that memory alone.
